elements.quote: to conduct a meta-analysis of global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states a meta-analysis was conducted but does not use the phrase 'systematic review' to identify the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: to conduct a meta-analysis of global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective: to perform a meta-analysis estimating the global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.

elements.quote: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang for cohort studies, case-control studies, and cross-sectional studies up to March 16, 2023, to conduct a meta-analysis of global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies included study designs (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) but does not state detailed exclusion criteria or other main inclusion/exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang ... up to March 16, 2023,
elements.reason: The abstract lists the information sources searched and reports the date through which searches were performed (March 16, 2023).

elements.quote: The risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states which tools were used to assess risk of bias in included studies.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, country, study type, and study population, and time-varying reinfection rates of SARS-CoV-2 were estimated using meta-regression.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the analytic methods used to present and synthesize results (meta-analysis, subgroup analyses, and meta-regression).

elements.quote: A total of 55 studies involving 111,846 cases of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection were included.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies and the number of reinfection cases, summarizing key study counts.

elements.quote: The pooled SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate was 0.94% (95% CI : 0.65 -1.35%).
elements.reason: The abstract presents the main outcome (pooled reinfection rate) and includes the number of studies/cases elsewhere in the abstract.

elements.quote: The pooled SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate was 0.94% (95% CI : 0.65 -1.35%).
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports the summary estimate with its 95% confidence interval.

elements.quote: SARS-CoV-2 is at risk of reinfection and the Omicron variant has a higher reinfection rate than other currently known variants.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect when comparing groups (Omicron has a higher reinfection rate than other variants) and which group is associated with higher rates.
The abstract does not briefly summarize limitations of the included evidence (risk of bias, inconsistency, or imprecision).

elements.quote: Meta-regression analysis found that the overall reinfection rate increased and then decreased over time, followed by a period of plateauing and then a trend of increasing and then decreasing... The results of this study could help guide public health measures and vaccination strategies in response to the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of results and states their implications for public health measures and vaccination strategies.
The abstract does not state the primary source of funding; funding is reported elsewhere in the paper but not in the abstract.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number (PROSPERO registration appears in the main text but is not included in the abstract).

elements.quote: Therefore, the aim of this study was to conduct a meta-analysis to describe and summarize the current reinfection rates in different regions and among diverse populations. Furthermore, the study sought to examine trends in reinfection rates over time, so as to provide reference for the development of global unified reinfection standards and reinfection measures in the future.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the study objectives: to describe and summarize reinfection rates across regions/populations and to examine time trends in reinfection rates.

elements.quote: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline(Ovid), Embase(Ovid), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure(CNKI), Wanfang using 'COVID-19' , '2019-nCoV' , 'SARS-COV-2' , 'Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2' , 'reinfection' , 'recurrence' , 'repeat positive' and 'repeat infections' as keywords, from January 1, 2020 to March 16, 2023 (Additional file 2).
elements.reason: The review targets observational studies reporting reinfection incidence (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) rather than intervention effects, so PICO-style planned comparisons for interventions are not applicable.

elements.quote: We searched for papers published on PubMed, Web of Science, Medline(Ovid), Embase(Ovid), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure(CNKI), Wanfang ... from January 1, 2020 to March 16, 2023 (Additional file 2).
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the date range of the searches and specifies the end date (March 16, 2023), which indicates when the sources were last searched/consulted.

elements.quote: "One of them reported only the reinfection rate, but not the associated number of first infections as well as the number of reinfections, and two other articles studied the same population, so the meta-analysis of single-group rates could not be performed. Therefore, we excluded the above literature with the number of unreported infections and selected one of two literature with the same population for inclusion."
elements.reason: The manuscript describes a specific decision rule for handling reports lacking necessary data (excluded) and for duplicate/same-population reports (selected one of the two), but does not provide comprehensive decision rules for other types of multiple reports or inconsistencies.

elements.quote: The complete information extracted included the first author, study period, country, study population, sample size, study design, reinfected variants, time between two positive tests (days), age, reinfection rate, and the number of reinfections.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists the outcome domains sought (reinfection rate, number of reinfections) and other extracted variables; additionally it provides a working definition of reinfection (>=90 days) in the same chunk, defining the outcome.

elements.quote: The complete information extracted included ... time between two positive tests (days), ... In addition, considering the change in the reinfection rate over time, we constructed a multiple meta-regression using the time interval between two positive tests as the independent variable, to estimate the time-varying reinfection rate.
elements.reason: The time frame/measurement for the outcome is specified as the time between two positive tests (days), and analyses were performed using that time interval to estimate time-varying reinfection rates.
No statement was found indicating whether all results compatible with each outcome domain (all measures, time points, analyses) were sought across studies.

No evidence was found reporting changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains or rationales for any such changes.

elements.quote: The complete information extracted included the first author, study period, country, study population, sample size, study design, reinfected variants, time between two positive tests (days), age, reinfection rate, and the number of reinfections.

elements.quote: If the paper did not mention the reinfection variant, we classified the reinfection variants based on the WHO standards according to the study period.
elements.reason: The authors describe an explicit assumption/approach used to handle missing information about reinfection variant, stating they classified variants based on WHO standards when not reported; they also describe use of online translator for non-English articles during screening.

elements.quote: Additional file 3: Information extraction form.
elements.reason: The supplement lists an 'Information extraction form' (Additional file 3), indicating a tool/form was used to determine data items; however, no citation or detailed description of this tool or its source is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: the summarized reinfection rate was approximately 0.94% (95% CI : 0.65 -1.35%).
elements.reason: The report explicitly presents the outcome as a reinfection rate (proportion) with 95% confidence intervals, indicating the effect measure used for the main outcome (pooled rate/proportion).
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect size (e.g., what constitutes small/large effect) or rationale for such thresholds are reported in the provided evidence.
There is no description in the provided evidence of methods used to re-express synthesized results using another effect measure (e.g., converting between odds ratios and risk ratios).

elements.quote: Meta-analysis is a method to obtain weighted average results from various studies. In addition to pooling effect sizes, meta-analysis can also be used to estimate disease frequencies, such as incidence and prevalence. However, when the rate is close to 0 or 1, two problems will occur in the meta-regression: the confidence interval may exceed the interval of 0-1, and the variance is squeezed towards 0. Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution. Four transformations were taken: log transformation, logit transformation, arcsine transformation, and double arcsine transformation. Through the hypothesis test after the transformation, we decided to use the logit transformation (see Additional file 5 for specific results).
elements.reason: The authors justify using meta-analysis to estimate disease frequency and explain why they transformed the proportion (issues when rates near 0 or 1) and why they selected the logit transformation. This provides justification for the chosen data transformation and handling of the effect measure (proportion), but does not fully justify the choice of effect measure type beyond using rates/proportions.

elements.quote: The inclusion criteria were: (1) Conformed to research questions, i.e., studies that estimated the reinfection rate of SARS-CoV-2 or we could calculate it based on the data provided in the paper; (2) The study design included cohort study, case-control study, and descriptive study; (3) The study fited our working definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. ... The exclusion criteria were: (1) The sample size was less than 20; (2) Belonged to one of the following types of studies: editorial, case report, case series study, systematic review, meta-analysis, animal experiment, news report; (3) Secondary reporting or articles on repeated studies of the same population; (4) Grey literature, including a range of documents not controlled by commercial publishing organizations. The reviewers independently (CY, Z-WH, H-XY, C-MS, LX, H-HP) screened the literature based on inclusion and exclusion criteria. Conflicts were resolved by other independent reviewers (ZT Y-CH). ... Subgroup analyses were performed by meta-regression to fit stratified rates of reinfection based on variables such as variant and country, and we also used spline regression to fit time-varying reinfection rates that did not account for heterogeneity.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states eligibility inclusion and exclusion criteria, describes independent screening and conflict resolution, and explains how studies were allocated to subgroup/meta-regression syntheses (e.g., by variant, country and time), which describes the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each synthesis.

elements.quote: Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution. Four transformations were taken: log transformation, logit transformation, arcsine transformation, and double arcsine transformation. Through the hypothesis test after the transformation, we decided to use the logit transformation (see Additional file 5 for specific results).
elements.reason: The methods for preparing outcome data for synthesis are explicitly described: the authors state they transformed reinfection rates to approximate normality, list four specific transformations considered, and report selecting the logit transformation based on hypothesis testing (with further details in a supplementary file).

elements.quote:

elements.reason: The manuscript includes Table 1 showing subgroup results with columns for article number, proportion, 95% CI, tau-squared, and P, demonstrating the tabular structure and the data included.

elements.quote: Fig. 5 Meta-regression of time-varying reinfection rates among health care workers (red dots indicate true values, shaded areas are 95% CI )
elements.reason: The manuscript describes graphical displays (e.g., meta-regression plots) and explains graphical elements (red dots as true values, shaded areas as 95% CI); forest plots are also referenced (Additional file 6).

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, reinfection variant, country, study population, and study type respectively, and the results were shown in Table 1, and forest plots for each subgroup analysis were shown in Additional file 6.
elements.reason: The basis for grouping studies (age, variant, country, study population, study type) is explicitly reported and linked to the tables and subgroup forest plots.

elements.quote: The forest plot was shown in Additional file 6. Subgroup analyses were performed for age, reinfection variant, country, study population, and study type respectively, and the results were shown in Table 1, and forest plots for each subgroup analysis were shown in Additional file 6.
elements.reason: No non-standard graphs are reported or justified; the manuscript refers to standard displays (forest plots, meta-regression plots, flow chart and tables) and provides no rationale for any non-standard graphical methods, so this conditional item does not apply.

elements.quote: All analyses were performed using R statistical software (version 4.2.3).
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the software and its version (R 4.2.3) but does not report specific R packages or their version numbers used for the statistical synthesis.

elements.quote: In contrast to meta-regression, the results of spline regression that did not account for heterogeneity showed an 'S-shaped' trend ... The difference between the results of spline regression and meta-regression may be due to the fact that the spline regression did not take into account the effects of different countries and reinfection variants on the reinfection rate, while the subgroup analysis in meta-analysis has shown that country and reinfection strains are important factors affecting the pooled reinfection rate.
elements.reason: The authors describe and justify use of spline regression (in addition to meta-regression) as an alternative approach to fit time-varying trends, and discuss differences and rationale between the approaches. They also note exclusion of studies that could not be meta-analysed (text_8).

elements.quote: Heterogeneity between studies was expressed using Cochran's Q statistic test (P < 0.05) as well as I 2 > 50%. If heterogeneity was low, a fixed-effects model was used to combine rates and correction estimates from different studies. Otherwise, a random-effects model was used.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies the models used (fixed-effect vs random-effects) and gives the rationale based on heterogeneity levels (Cochran's Q and I2 thresholds).

elements.quote: We used meta-analysis to evaluate the pooled rate of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection in the included studies. ... Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution. Four transformations were taken: log transformation, logit transformation, arcsine transformation, and double arcsine transformation. Through the hypothesis test after the transformation, we decided to use the logit transformation (see Additional file 5 for specific results).
elements.reason: The statistical methods are reported: meta-analysis, meta-regression, subgroup analyses, and specific data transformations (logit chosen) applied prior to pooling rates.

elements.quote: Heterogeneity between studies was expressed using Cochran's Q statistic test ( P < 0.05) as well as I 2 > 50%.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the statistical methods used to identify and quantify heterogeneity (Cochran's Q and I2 threshold).
No between-study variance estimator (e.g., DerSimonian-Laird, REML) for random-effects meta-analysis is specified in the provided evidence.
The method used to calculate confidence intervals for the summary effect in random-effects meta-analysis is not reported in the available excerpts.
No additional implementation details for random-effects models (e.g., weighting scheme, small-sample corrections) are provided in the retrieved evidence.
No Bayesian meta-analysis was performed or described in the manuscript, so reporting of prior distributions is not applicable.
The manuscript does not describe any methods to account for statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: One of them reported only the reinfection rate, but not the associated number of first infections as well as the number of reinfections, and two other articles studied the same population, so the meta-analysis of single-group rates could not be performed. Therefore, we excluded the above literature with the number of unreported infections and selected one of two literature with the same population for inclusion.
elements.reason: The authors identify planned syntheses that were impossible (e.g., studies without required data or duplicate populations), and provide reasons for exclusion.

elements.quote: we constructed a multiple meta-regression using the time interval between two positive tests as the independent variable, to estimate the time-varying reinfection rate. Subgroup analyses were performed by meta-regression to fit stratified rates of reinfection based on variables such as variant and country, and we also used spline regression to fit time-varying reinfection rates that did not account for heterogeneity.
elements.reason: The methods used to explore heterogeneity are explicitly described: subgroup analyses, multiple meta-regression (with time interval as independent variable), and spline regression.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, reinfection variant, country, study population, and study type respectively... Table 1 Results of subgroup analysis ... Reinfected variants: Wild, Alpha, Delta, Omicron; Country: the United States, the United Kingdom, Türkiye, Italy, India, Iran, Israel, Spain, Canada, Brazil, Denmark; Study type: cohort study, case-control study, cross- sectional study
elements.reason: Factors and their levels are reported and shown in Table 1 (age groups, variants, countries, study populations, study types). However, the authors do not state any pre-specified expected direction of effect modification.

elements.quote: we constructed a multiple meta-regression using the time interval between two positive tests as the independent variable, to estimate the time-varying reinfection rate. Subgroup analyses were performed by meta-regression to fit stratified rates of reinfection based on variables such as variant and country
elements.reason: The text explicitly states a meta-regression was constructed using study-level variables (time interval, variant, country) as predictors, indicating the analyses used study-level variables.

No explicit description is provided of the statistical methods used to compare subgroup effects (e.g., tests for interaction or procedures to compare subgroup estimates) in the retrieved methods or results text.

elements.quote: In contrast to meta-regression, the results of spline regression that did not account for heterogeneity showed an 'S-shaped' trend in total reinfection and in the subgroup with the general population... The difference between the results of spline regression and meta-regression may be due to the fact that the spline regression did not take into account the effects of different countries and reinfection variants on the reinfection rate

elements.quote: However, the limitations of this study are as follows: first, we did not include the 'grey literature' , which may lack potential relevant studies that meet the inclusion criteria [35]. In addition, the pattern of publication bias in the field of single-arm study with single-group rate is not clear, and funnel plot analysis may lead to inaccurate conclusions. Second, there is still no clear global definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. In the literature of reinfection searched in this study, most of the diagnostic criteria were at least 90 days between two positive laboratory tests. In order to avoid data heterogeneity in metaanalysis while ensuring data quantity, we used previous literature and previous definitions of reinfection in some countries as the criteria for included literature and data extraction in this study. Although we noted that clinical symptoms and real time-PCR or Rapid Antigen test were also important for the definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection, forming a globally harmonized standard definition was definitely beyond the scope of this study. Besides, due to the lack of specific data in the included literature, subgroup analysis of disease severity and vaccination could not be carried out, so it was impossible to explore all the sources of heterogeneity of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rates. Meanwhile, the sample sizes of the literature included in this study were quite different, which might also be the source of heterogeneity in reinfection rates.
